Build something worth keeping.

An implementation proposal. A new research direction. A mathematical argument that survives scrutiny. The mission is useful progress; models and methods can improve as the project grows.

  1. Define useful workFix the outcome before choosing the method.
  2. Level 3 · Meta-strategic intelligenceDiscover, test, combine and improve the strategies themselves.

Computer Use connects reasoning to visible screen work. Today’s native runner operates a bounded disposable browser; reviewed code execution, proof tools, broader desktops and settlement each require their own connection.

01 · FIND AN OPPORTUNITY WORTH BUILDING

A value hypothesis, to test against real usefulness, full costs and alternatives. No income or savings are established by preparing a mission.

Add known facts, assumptions, constraints and resources. This text becomes visible in the work surface and stays with this attempt; assumptions are not external evidence.

Keep this acceptance contract unchanged when comparing strategies. A different outcome starts a new comparison.

Use public, non-personal material that you have permission to use. The configured runner reads the exact approved URLs; it cannot log into private accounts.

02 · Improve the strategy. Challenge the frame.

The starting approaches are editable seeds. Ask the configured model to discover, test, combine and refine alternatives, then explain what could change the game while preserving the useful outcome.

Explain why the alternative still achieves the required outcome. A new framing is a hypothesis until its result has been reviewed.

03 · Execution setup and advanced controls

Current native execution uses a disposable, screenshot-driven Chromium workspace. It can read approved public material and create visible work products. Code execution, performance measurements and formal proof checking require separately qualified tools; proposals remain unverified until tested.

Use your operator’s current qualified model

Select the model and immutable container during native execution. No API key belongs in this workspace.

Preparation is free and makes no model call. A configured native executor and provider account perform the work. The saved mission and returned evidence stay together in your project.

Import computer-return.json from the runner’s output directory. Import preserves a historical result. Provider completion is a claim; inspect the screenshots and actual deliverable before reviewing it.

        A few things worth knowing.
        What can I do for free?
        Develop a valuable mission, compare its proposed strategies and save your workspace for free. The configured native executor performs Computer Use work through its model provider. A maintained catalog example is also available as a local engineering tool.
        What counts as Alpha here?
        Alpha is the useful advantage you can demonstrate for a concrete opportunity. An attractive proposal, generated code or mathematical argument is a candidate: test the actual result, review the evidence and account for full costs before claiming value.
        What do I keep?
        You control the files you download: a workspace, reusable code, inputs, output and project history. Included code is Apache 2.0; bundled AGI Jobs components retain their MIT license. Input rights and any rights in commissioned or third-party work remain yours to establish.
        Does this certify Specialist ASI or authorize deployment?
        No. This is a working, bounded local demonstration. Independent evaluation on protected fresh work and explicit accountable authorization are separate steps. The Gym develops capability; it does not certify it.
